title: SYSK's 2017 Super Spooktacular!
summary: Halloween special of Stuff You Should Know, ad-free as usual. Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with an update on Ed Grabowski's 2016 story "Extra Terrestrial"-style tale "Invocation" (transcribed as "Extrane of Use Invocot"), now being adapted into a film called The Between with a crowdfunding campaign and a targeted February 14, 2018 release. They then read Grabowski's new story "Gifts," about a housekeeper at the Shipped in Grange hotel who is terrorized by a disturbed child, Bobby, and a figure called Mr. Sorrow, ending with a phone call and a fall from a window. After a break, Josh and Chuck discuss Charlotte Perkins Gilman's 1892 feminist horror story "The Yellow Wallpaper," about a woman confined to a nursery by her physician husband, and then read the story aloud, ending with her creeping free and her husband fainting. The hosts close with social media and website information.

segments.title: Halloween opening and Ed Grabowski update
segments.summary: Hosts banter, explain the ad-free Halloween special format, and give an update on Ed Grabowski's prior story being adapted into the film The Between, with a crowdfunding campaign and a planned February 2018 release.

segments.title: Reading: Gifts by Ed Grabowski
segments.summary: A dramatized reading of the new horror story Gifts. A housekeeper hired at Shipped in Grange meets a boy, Bobby, who gives her eerie objects, including a burial casket pillow, coins, a blade, and scissors. Bobby is injured after falling from a window, and the housekeeper receives a disturbing phone call from her husband's line.

segments.title: Reactions to Gifts and transition
segments.summary: Hosts react to the story, praise its creepiness and short-film potential, and tease a break before the next reading.

segments.title: Eight-minute commercial break
segments.summary: The hosts mention an eight-minute commercial break before the next story.

segments.title: Introduction to The Yellow Wallpaper
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Charlotte Perkins Gilman's The Yellow Wallpaper, first published in New England Magazine, and discuss it as early feminist literature critiquing the treatment of women.

segments.title: Reading: The Yellow Wallpaper
segments.summary: Dramatized reading of Gilman's story. A narrator, prescribed a rest cure by her physician husband John, is confined to a nursery with yellow wallpaper, becomes fixated on a figure behind the pattern, and eventually tears the paper off and creeps around the room. When John breaks in, she declares she has gotten out and he faints.

segments.title: Reactions and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts react to the reading, note its feminist themes, wish listeners a happy Halloween, and give social media, email, and website information.
